title: mini-batch failure breadcrumbs
content:
TL;DR: Starting 2025-11-12 ~02:10 UTC we saw a ~30-50% drop in tokens/sec for a small set of customers. Root cause appears tied to continuous batching misconfiguration + a fallback path that disables batching under certain sequence patterns. Notes below are scratchpad breadcrumbs of commands tried, logs, quick repro steps, hypotheses, and next steps.

Observed impact
- Affected pool: prod-dedicated-gpupool-7 (nv4a)
- Customer impact: sustained token/sec drop on medium-length streaming requests (avg seq_len 256–512).
- Metrics: tokens/sec for route /v1/generate dropped from 12k -> 7.5k (p50 throughput) across pool on 2025-11-12 02:08–02:20 UTC. p95 latency increased from 220ms -> 480ms.

Timeline (quick)
- 2025-11-12 01:58 UTC: Canary deploy of serving-runtime v1.78.1 (rolling) — contains batching heuristics tweak (feature flag: BATCHER_CONTINUOUS_WINDOW_MS default changed 2 -> 1).
- 2025-11-12 02:06 UTC: Alerts for latency/throughput hit SLO thresholds.
- 2025-11-12 02:10 UTC: I started capturing logs and did quick revert tests.

Commands & snippets I ran (ordered approximate)
- Check pod health and restarts:
  kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o wide
  kubectl -n prod describe pod serving-runtime-7f8d9 -n prod
- Tail logs (main + batcher):
  kubectl -n prod logs serving-runtime-7f8d9 -c runtime --since=30m | grep -i batch | tail -200
  # observed many lines like:
  # WARN continuous_batcher: batch window shrunk to 1ms, emitting singletons
  # DEBUG batcher: enqueue latency=2ms batch_size=1 reason=window_timeout
- Grab runtime metrics snapshot (prometheus endpoint):
  curl -s http://serving-runtime-7f8d9:9100/metrics | egrep 'tokens_per_sec|batch_size_histogram|continuous_batch_window_ms'
  # before patch: batch_size_histogram_bucket{le="4"} 120000
  # after patch: batch_size_histogram_bucket{le="4"} 540000 (shift toward tiny batches)
- Repro with local load generator (toy):
  python tools/loadgen/send_concurrent.py --host=https://api.redwood.test --route=/v1/generate --concurrency=24 --seq_len=320 --duration=120
  # baseline run (v1.77) -> 11.8k tokens/sec
  # repro run (v1.78.1) -> 7.6k tokens/sec, batch sizes reported 1-2 most of the time
- Inspect feature flag state in configmap and env on pods:
  kubectl -n prod get configmap runtime-flags -o yaml | grep -A3 BATCHER_CONTINUOUS_WINDOW_MS
  # configmap had value '1' (ms). Older default was '2' in stable deploys.
- Look for fallbacks in codepaths (local grep):
  rg "disable_continuous_batching|force_singleton" -n serving-runtime | sed -n '1,120p'
  # found: if sequence has token_type != TEXT then force_singleton=true (to avoid KV cache collisions)

Error snippets and interesting log lines
- WARN continuous_batcher: window lowered to 1ms due to config override (caller=feature-flag-manager)
- DEBUG batch_dispatcher: fallback to direct_executor for request id=... reason=kv_cache_conflict
- ERROR kv_cache: inconsistent prefix state for key=abc123, invalidating local cache entry
- INFO perf: kernel-path=small-batch, cuda-graphs=disabled (reason=min_batch_size  > observed_batch_size)
- Stack-ish sample: (from runtime core log)
  at batcher::dispatch (batcher.cpp:324)
  at runtime::handle_request (serve.cpp:118)
  at main (main.cpp:42)

Quick diffs I inspected
- v1.77 -> v1.78.1:
  - BATCHER_CONTINUOUS_WINDOW_MS: 2 -> 1 (ms)
  - batching.cost_estimator: new param 'penalty_for_kv_conflict' default 0.1 added
  - small optimization: treat non-text token types as unsafe for shared KV cache (introduces fallback)

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Aggressive continuous-batcher window change (1ms) increased probability of singleton batches for medium-length streams -> causes kernels to choose small-batch execution path (higher per-token overhead). Evidence: batch size histogram shifted and logs indicating small-batch kernel path.
2) New KV-safety guard flips many mixed-token requests into force_singleton path due to upstream client sending occasional structured tokens (function calls). That reduces effective batching. Evidence: logs show kv_cache invalidation and direct_executor fallback.
3) Combined effect: shorter window + KV-safety fallback interacts synergistically so once a pod sees a few fallbacks its runtime enters a degraded steady state (CUDA graphs=false, caches cold).
4) There may also be a scheduling/regulator bug where small batches prevent continuous batching from filling due to clock tick misalignment on nv4a drivers (low-prob). No direct evidence yet.

Quick experiments run and results
- Revert feature flag to 2ms on a single pod (manually patched configmap + rolling restart): throughput on that pod recovered to ~11.4k tokens/sec (within noise).
- Toggled 'penalty_for_kv_conflict' to 0 (was 0.1) -> small recovery (~+10%).
- Forced kv_cache to skip validation (DEV build) -> recovered but unacceptable for prod correctness.

Reproduce steps (minimal)
1) Deploy runtime v1.78.1 with BATCHER_CONTINUOUS_WINDOW_MS=1 against a pod in staging with traffic that mixes TEXT and FUNCTION tokens (use function-calling sample).
2) Run loadgen: python tools/loadgen/send_concurrent.py --concurrency=24 --seq_len=320 --mixed-token-prob=0.15 --duration=300
3) Watch metrics: batch_size histogram, tokens_per_sec, cuda_graphs_enabled gauge.

Immediate mitigation applied
- Rolled back BATCHER_CONTINUOUS_WINDOW_MS to 2ms cluster-wide (hotfix configmap) at 2025-11-12 03:05 UTC -> CPU/GPU throughput returned to baseline across pools.
- Raised an incident ticket ENG-1423 and pinned responsible PR.

Longer-term fixes and notes
- Make window change a canary-local flag with auto-bisect tooling for batcher params.
- Add metric that tracks number of 'force_singleton' fallbacks per pod and alert when >1% of requests.
- Revisit KV-safety logic: consider shared KV cache versioning or typed-kv namespaces to avoid conservative fallbacks.
- Improve unit and e2e tests: synthetic mixed-token traffic should be part of canary suite.

Next steps (for me)
- Write a small regression test for the continuous-batcher that simulates mixed-token streams and asserts average batch_size > 3 under normal load. (TODO: add to /tools/test-batcher)
- Follow up with Priya on improving metrics for 'direct_executor' fallbacks and with Tomás on alternative KV namespacing approaches.
- Bake a small chaos probe that toggles BATCHER_CONTINUOUS_WINDOW_MS on canaries to detect regressions automatically.

Notes to self / loose thoughts
- Why did the cluster reach a steady degraded state rather than auto-recover? Possible warm/cold cache hysteresis: once CUDA graphs disabled and KV cold, warmup cost is big and continuous batching has less headroom to aggregate.
- Consider a guard that avoids permanently disabling cuda-graphs until X seconds of sustained small batches.

Snippets to include in incident postmortem (copy/paste friendly)
- kubectl commands we used for hotfix:
  kubectl -n prod get configmap runtime-flags -o yaml > /tmp/flags.yaml
  sed -i 's/BATCHER_CONTINUOUS_WINDOW_MS: 1/BATCHER_CONTINUOUS_WINDOW_MS: 2/' /tmp/flags.yaml
  kubectl -n prod apply -f /tmp/flags.yaml
  kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/serving-runtime
- Loadgen command we used:
  python tools/loadgen/send_concurrent.py --host=https://staging.api.redwood --route=/v1/generate --concurrency=24 --seq_len=320 --mixed-token-prob=0.12 --duration=180

Open questions
- Does the runtime expose a per-request tag that marks "forced_singleton" so downstream metrics can slice by customer? (If not, add it.)
- Can we make the KV fallback less binary? e.g., try joiner with isolation namespace before forcing singleton.

Bottom line: quick rollback of continuous-batcher window fixed the customer-visible regression. Root cause is an interaction between a more aggressive batching window and conservative KV-safety fallback that together reduced effective batching and forced small-kernel paths. This doc is a scratchpad for follow-ups.

---
notes-end
